prompt: A good study plan divides a large amount of work into smaller, manageable tasks. Trying to learn everything in a single evening can leave a student tired and confused. Short study sessions spread over several days allow time to review difficult ideas and notice what is still unclear. To make a useful plan,

lt.label: LT-8
lt.continuation:
find out how much time you have before the test. If you are studying for an exam on a specific topic, it may help to know where you are at.
- Keep in mind that the more time spent doing something, the easier it will be to get better.
- Try to break down your work into small groups rather than attempting to do too many things at once.
- Study in a comfortable place with adequate light.
- Take a daily break, but don’t try to cram too much work into one night.
The best way to learn is to take advantage of opportunities to practice. For instance:
- Find a tutor for your subject.
- Study the material as close as possible.
- Practice on a test at home or at school.
Take note of your own progress and look for ways to learn more effectively.
- You may want to check the syllabus beforehand to see if there are any specific things you need to do at the start of each unit.
- Try reading an article about the subject before you go to class.
- Take notes when you are studying.
- Use questions from the syllabus to get your head around key points.
- Read the material until you understand it completely.
For more guidance on effective study methods, see the following articles from Cambridge University Press
